title: Progress and prospects of metal–organic framework-based materials for sodium-ion batteries
content: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have shown promising potential as an alternative to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for sustainable energy storage. SIBs are desirable alternatives for future energy storage technologies due to the widespread availability and low price of sodium. However, slow diffusion kinetics, limited electrode compatibility, and structural instability result from the larger ionic radius of Na+, all of which hinder electrochemical performance. The use of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) in batteries is one strategy that has been explored to overcome these barriers. Due to their high porosity, tunable structures, flexible chemical architectures, and large specific surface area, MOFs have been widely used in applications such as sensors, drug delivery, and gas adsorption. There have also been numerous reports of their derivatives being used as battery electrode materials. The fundamentals, crystal structures, characteristics, and synthesis of MOFs are first addressed in this article. The latest developments in MOF-based materials used as electrolytes, anodes, cathodes, and separators for SIBs are then addressed. Lastly, a brief discussion of the challenges and future potential paths of MOF application in SIBs is provided.
